title: WPSS/2514/2019 of PANKAJ DIMRI Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

COURT'S OR JUDGES'S ORDERS
WPSS No. 2513 of 2019
WPSS No. 2514 of 2019
WPSS No. 2515 of 2019
WPSS No. 2516 of 2019
WPSS No. 2518 of 2019
WPSS No. 2545 of 2019
Hon 'b le Man oj Ku m ar Tiw ar i, J.

Mr. Vinay Kum ar, Advocate for the
petitioners.
Mr. P.C. Bisht, Additional Chief
Standing Counsel for the State of
Uttarakhand.
Heard learned counsel for the
parties.
 Petitioners were appointed as
Constable in Uttarakhand Police under
sports quota between 2006 to 2010.
By m eans of these writ petitions,
petitioners have sought the following
relief:
"I . I ssue a writ, order or direction in the nature
of Mandam us directing the respondents to
consider and grant the out of turn promotion to
the petitioners on the post of Head Constable
under the provisions of Out of Turn Promotion
Policy 2008 notified vide Office Mem orandum
dated 13th August 2008 inasmuch as the
petitioners were eligible and qualified under the
said policy at the relevant point of tim e for out
of turn promotion, but were wrongly denied the
same."
I n sum & substance, petitioners are
seeking enforcem ent of a Government
Policy contained in Office Mem orandum
dated 13.08.2008, which provided for
out of turn prom otion to skilled
sportspersons. According to the
petitioners, they were eligible to be

considered for prom otion in term s of said
policy, as they have secured Silver or
Bronze Medals in All I ndia Police Sports
events.
I t is not in dispute that the Office
Mem orandum dated 13.08.2008 was
superseded by Statutory Rules framed
under Section 87 of Uttarakhand Police
Act, 2007, notified on 03.09.2016.
Petitioners are ineligible for out of turn
prom otion under the said Rules,
therefore, they contend that their claim
for out of turn prom otion should be
considered under the policy contained in
Office Memorandum dated 13.08.2008.
Learned counsel for the petitioners
contends that sim ilarly situate persons
were given out of turn prom otion vide
order dated 13.07.2019, however, those
persons had approached this Court in
2013 by filing WPSS No. 1404 of 2013,
which was disposed by learned Single
Judge vide order dated 26.09.2013,
directing the Com petent Authority to
take decision in their matter, in
accordance with existing Government
Policy, within six weeks. The Special
Appeal filed by the State Government
against the said order was dismissed by
Division Bench of this Court and,
thereafter, Hon'ble Suprem e Court also
dismissed the S.L.P. filed by the State
Government, on 05.07.2019. Petitioners
have approached this Court only in 2019
when som e persons were given out of
turn prom otion in term s of order passed
in WPSS No. 1404 of 2013. Thus,
petitioners are fence-sitters, who filed
these writ petitions three years after
enforcement of the Rules dealing with
out of turn promotion.
Learned counsel for the petitioners

contends that out of turn prom otions
were not given to anyone between 2011
to 2013, consequently, a valuable right
of out of turn prom otion was denied to
them.
I n paragraph no. 7 of the counter
affidavit, explanation for not granting out
of turn prom otion to sportsperson after
2010 has been given, which is extracted
below:
"7. That in reply to the contents of para 9 of the
writ petition it is submitted that since in the
office memo dated 13-08-2008, issued by the
State Government, the standard prescribed
regarding granting of out of turn promotion to
the skilled players were very easy and
considering the regular increase in the number
of posts due to promotion as well as in view of
the difficulty to the Government in adjusting the
promotional posts with a view to amend the
G.O. dated 13-08-2008 vide office letter no.
DG-7-166/ 2004 dated 04-01-2011 the Police
Headquarter, Dehradun sent a new proposal to
the Government, wherein the condition of
demotion of the skilled players in case of non-performing well in future is also included and
since no amendment has been made by the
State Government on the proposal sent by the
Police Headquarter vide office letter dated 4-1-
2011 for the proposed amendment and the said
proposal for the proposed amendment
remained pending before the State
Government, therefore, after 2011 the
Uttarakhand Police Department did not initiated
proceeding for granting the out of turn
promotion to the skilled players/ employees on
the basis of the office memo dated 13-08-2008
(proposal for amendment).
I t is further submitted before the Hon'ble Court
that the petitioners secured the medals in the
year 2012-2013 and the petitioners never

moved any application for granting out of turn
promotion at that relevant point of when the
G.O. dated 13-08-2008 was in existence and
after the laps of period of 09 years the
petitioners have filed the instant writ petition
for granting out of turn promotion on the basis
of the Government order dated 13-08-2008
whereas the said Government order dated 13-
08-2008 has now been superseded by the
notification no. 1169/ XX-1/ 2016-1(36) 2007
dated 03-09-2016 issued by the State
Government and as of now for granting out of
turn promotion to the skilled player in the police
department "The Uttarakhand Police Skilled
Player Out of Turn Promotion Proceeding Rules,
2016" is in existence."
Learned counsel for the petitioners
has relied upon a judgm ent rendered by
Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of
Y.V. Rangaiah Vs. J. Sreenivasa
Rao, reported in (1983) 3 SCC 284, in
support of his contention that vacancies
in the prom otional posts occurring prior
to enforcem ent of 2016 Rules have to be
filled up in accordance with the policy in
vogue before enforcement of Rules.
Paragraph no. 9 of the said judgm ent is
reproduced below:
"9 . Having heard the counsel for the parties, we
find no force in either of the two contentions.
Under the old rules a panel had to be prepared
every year in September. Accordingly, a panel
should have been prepared in the year 1976
and transfer or promotion to the post of Sub-Registrar Grade I I should have been made out
of that panel. I n that event the petitioners in
the two representation petitions who ranked
higher than Respondents 3 to 15 would not
have been deprived of their right of being
considered for promotion. The vacancies which
occurred prior to the amended rules would be
governed by the old rules and not by the
amended rules. I t is adm itted by counsel for

both the parties that henceforth promotion to
the post of Sub-Registrar Grade I I will be
according to the new rules on the zonal basis
and not on the State-wide basis and, therefore,
there was no question of challenging the new
rules. But the question is of filling the vacancies
that occurred prior to the amended rules. We
have not the slightest doubt that the posts
which fell vacant prior to the amended rules
would be governed by the old rules and not by
the new rules."
I n the hum ble opinion of this Court,
the said judgment does not support the
case of the petitioners. I t is not the case
of the petitioners that the vacancies
earm arked for out of turn prom otion
between 2011 to 2016 are still available.
There is no pleading in the writ petition
regarding the num ber of such vacancies
or year wise breakup of vacancies. I n
fact, the sole contention of the
petitioners is that as they were eligible
for out of turn promotion under the
policy contained in Office Mem orandum
dated 13.08.2008, therefore, their
eligibility cannot be taken away by the
Rules enforced in 2016.
Hon'ble Supreme Court in a recent
judgment rendered in the case of State
of Him achal Pradesh & others Vs. Raj
Kum ar & others, reported in 2022 SCC
Online SC 680, after considering the
entire law on the subject has
sum m arized the legal position in
paragraph no. 70, which is reproduced
below:
"7 0 . A review of the fifteen cases that have
distinguished Rangaiah would demonstrate that
this Court has been consistently carving out
exceptions to the broad proposition formulated
in Rangaiah. The findings in these judgments,
that have a direct bearing on the proposition
formulated by Rangaiah are as under:

1. There is no rule of universal application that
vacancies must be necessarily filled on the
basis of the law which existed on the date when
they arose, Rangaiah's case must be
understood in the context of the rules involved
therein.
2. I t is now a settled proposition of law that a
candidate has a right to be considered in the
light of the existed rules, which im plies the
"rule in force" as on the date consideration
takes place. The right to be considered for
promotion occurs on the date of consideration
of the eligible candidates.
3. The Government is entitled to take a
conscious policy decision not to fill up the
vacancies arising prior to the amendment of the
rules. The employee does not acquire any
vested right to being considered for promotion
in accordance with the repealed rules in view of
the policy decision taken by the
Government. There is no obligation for the
Government to make appointments as per the
old rules in the event of restructuring of the
cadre is intended for efficient working of the
unit. The only requirement is that the policy
decisions of the Government must be fair and
reasonable and must be justified on the
touchstone of Article 14.
4. The principle in Rangaiah need not be applied
merely because posts were created, as it is not
obligatory for the appointing authority to fill up
the posts immediately.
5. When there is no statutory duty cast upon
the State to consider appointments to vacancies
that existed prior to the amendment, the State
cannot be directed to consider the cases."
I n view of the legal position as
explained by Hon'ble Suprem e Court in
the case of Himachal Pradesh & others
Vs. Raj Kum ar & others (Supra), a
candidate has a right to be considered
for prom otion in the light of existing
Rules or the Rules, which are in force on
the date of when exercise for prom otion
takes place. Thus, the contention raised

by learned counsel for the petitioners
that petitioners have a vested right to be
considered for prom otion as per the
Office Mem orandum dated 13.08.2008,
even after supersession of the said Office
Mem orandum by Statutory Rules, cannot
be accepted.
Learned counsel for the petitioners
then contended that State Governm ent
had granted relaxation to certain persons
by invoking Rule 19 of out of turn
prom otion Rules, 2016. I n support of
this contention, he has relied upon a
com munication issued by I nspector
General (Personnel) dated 25.10.2017,
which is Annexure No. 7 to the writ
petition.
Perusal of the said docum ent,
however, reveals that the relaxation
granted to those persons is different
from the relaxation which petitioners are
claiming. Moreover, the said relaxation
was granted in terms of order of this
Court passed in Contem pt Petition No.
425 of 2015. Thus, petitioners cannot
claim any benefit based on relaxation
granted to other persons, who were
prom oted in term s of order of this Court.
Thus, while holding that petitioners
do not have any vested right for out of
turn prom otion, this Court thinks that
ends of justice would be m et, if
petitioners are permitted to approach the
Competent Authority, by m aking
representation.
Accordingly, the writ petitions are
disposed of by permitting the petitioners
to m ake representation to respondent
no. 2, within three weeks' from today. I f
they submit representation within
stipulated tim e, decision thereupon shall
be taken as per law within a period of

three m onths' from the date of receipt of
representation(s) with certified copy of
this order.

( Man oj Ku m ar Tiw ar i, J.)
 18.10.2022
Arpan
